newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-TUCKER HOMERS TWICE AS SMOLTZ WINS FOR BRAVES.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-TUCKER HOMERS TWICE AS SMOLTZ WINS FOR BRAVES.

text.p: Michael Tucker homered twice and drove in four runs and John Smoltz pitched seven scoreless innings as the Atlanta Braves trounced the Philadelphia Phillies 9-1 on Saturday.
Chipper Jones and Javy Lopez also homered for Atlanta, winner of four in a row.
Smoltz (7-7) allowed six hits to snap a personal four-game losing streak. He walked two and struck out seven in the first game since April 15 that he did not allow a run.
Curt Schilling (9-7) struck out 12 but was drilled for seven runs and eight hits -- four of them homers -- in 5 2/3 innings. He has a league-leading 151 strikeouts this season.

"It picked me up today, it was a much-needed game against a pitcher of Schilling's quality," said Smoltz, last season's Cy Young Award winner who has struggled this year. "I told myself to keep making quality pitches and sooner or later it would work out."

Tucker opened the scoring by slamming a 2-0 offering from Schilling over the left-centre field fence in the first inning. In the third, he belted a three-run shot over the right-field fence for a 4-0 Braves' lead.
"A loss is a loss, whether you strike out one or 15," said Schilling after the Phils suffered their fifth consecutive defeat and 13th in the last 14 games.
In Chicago, Mark Grace and Sammy Sosa each hit two-run homers and rookie Jeremi Gonzalez allowed two runs on two hits over 6 1/3 innings as the Cubs beat the Houston Astros 5-2.

Gonzalez (4-2), coming off his first major league shutout Tuesday at St Louis, gave up both runs in the seventh before getting help from Kent Bottenfield, who struck out Jeff Bagwell with the bases loaded.

Grace celebrated his 33rd birthday with a homer in the first off Ramon Garcia (3-6). Sosa, who Friday signed a four-year contract extension worth over $42 million, connected for his 16th in the eighth off John Hudek.
In Los Angeles, Steve Finley homered twice and drove in three runs and Tony Gwynn added a two-run homer to lead the San Diego Padres to a 9-3 thumping of the Dodgers.
Pete Smith pitched five innings in his first start since 1995 for the win. Hideo Nomo (7-7) surrendered a season-high six runs and eight hits in 4 2/3 innings to suffer the loss.
Finley, who hit three homers Monday at San Francisco and one Thursday in the series opener, belted a solo shot in the first and a two-run dinger in the sixth.
Ex-Dodger Carlos Hernandez added a two-run double for San Diego. Gwynn has nine RBI in his last three games.
In Cincinnati, Willie McGee and Dmitri Young combined for eight hits, five RBI and a pair of steals to lead the St Louis Cardinals to a 12-6 victory over the Reds.
McGee and Young each had four hits. McGee drove in three runs and Young knocked in a pair.
Ron Gant contributed a two-run shot in the first inning to the Cards' 18-hit attack.

John Smiley (5-10) was ripped for seven runs and eight hits in 2 1/3 innings to tie Fernando Valenzuela, who started for St Louis, for the league lead in losses. Mark Petkovsek (3-4) tossed four scoreless innings for the win.

At Florida, Livan Hernandez allowed two runs and three hits in five innings to earn his his first major league win as the Marlins beat the Montreal Expos 4-2 to retain sole possessino of second place in the National League East.
Hernandez (1-0), a 22-year-old Cuban defector, walked two and struck out six in his second start of the season.
Gary Sheffield doubled home Edgar Renteria in a two-run first inning and Renteria doubled and scored on a sacrifice fly by Jim Eisenreich in the third.
Jim Bullinger (5-7) took the loss, giving up three runs on four hits in six innings.
In Pittsburgh, Armando Reynoso allowed two runs over 6 2/3 innings and Bernard Gilkey, John Olerud and Luis Lopez each drove in two runs as the New York Mets beat the Pirates 8-3.
Reynoso (6-1) gave up six hits and did not issue a walk. Esteban Loaiza (5-5) held New York scoreless before tiring in the sixth. He allowed three runs and six hits in six innings.
Olerud had RBI doubles and scored in both the sixth and eighth innings and Bernard Gilkey delivered a two-run single in the sixth.
The Mets blew open a 3-2 game when Lopez capped a five-run seventh with a two-run triple.
At Colorado, Dante Bichette belted two homers and drove in six runs and Kevin Ritz threw a six-hitter for his first complete game in a year as the Rockies hammered the San Francisco Giants 9-2.
Bichette hit a three-run blast off starter Mark Gardner (8-4) in the first and added a three-run shot in the third off Gardner to give the Rockies a commanding 6-1 lead.
Larry Walker added his 23rd homer and Vinny Castilla belted his 20th for Colorado.
Ritz (6-7) gave up two runs, including a solo homer by J.T. Snow in the second.
